topic: Airspace, ATZ, MATZ and transponders (Skyway Code)
summary: An ATZ is a cylinder of 2 NM radius when the longest runway is 1,850 m or less, 2.5 NM otherwise, extending 2,000 ft above the aerodrome. A MATZ is not controlled airspace for civilians but contact is strongly recommended. Most UK GA controlled airspace is class D (CTRs and CTAs) with class A for airways and TMAs. Transponders should be on with altitude reporting (squawk 7000 VFR), and Mode S is needed in class A and C, above FL100 and in TMZs. Built from the Skyway Code pp.68-72 and 84-89.
src: The Skyway Code (CAP 1535 v4, Nov 2023), pp.68-72, 84-89
sections: Airspace structure
ICAO classes A to G exist but in UK airspace A, C, D, E and G are notified
Class A: IFR only, clearance required, ATC service and separation for all flights
Most controlled airspace GA meets is class D: CTRs (surface to about 2,500 ft AMSL or higher) and CTAs (base about 1,500 ft AMSL, overlying CTRs)
TMAs cover several busy aerodromes and are normally class A (the Scottish TMA is an exception)
Airways link structures and are normally class A. Some in Scotland are class E with a transponder mandatory zone, giving VFR access without clearance
In class D there is no formal ATC separation of VFR from other traffic, only traffic information
ATZ and aerodromes without one
An ATZ is a cylinder around an aerodrome: 2 NM radius if the longest runway is 1,850 m or less, 2.5 NM if longer, up to 2,000 ft above the aerodrome
You may cross an ATZ en route if you comply with Rule 11: with ATC permission is needed, with AFIS or AGCS get information
Some aerodromes without an ATZ are shown with a circle and T (intensive training) or U (unusual activity such as aerobatics or formation)
MATZ
A MATZ is not controlled airspace for civilians but contains high-performance military aircraft, so contact the unit before entering
It contains an ATZ: never enter that ATZ without a positive clearance
Standard MATZ: 5 NM radius, 3,000 ft above airfield level, with two STUBS and LARS frequency
Request a 'MATZ penetration service' about 10 minutes flying time ahead. If there is no reply after two attempts you may enter with caution
MATZ are often inactive at weekends but check. Downwind and base legs of the radar training circuit can lie outside the MATZ
Requesting a transit
Start with the request: for example 'Solent Radar, G-DOME, request Basic Service and zone transit'
On 'pass your message', give type, route, position, altitude and QNH. 'Standby' needs no acknowledgement
Read back the squawk, altitude limits and service, and acknowledge future instructions with 'wilco'
Remain clear until cleared. If no clearance is likely, alter course away positively
Transponder
Squawk 7000 VFR or 2000 IFR. Select Mode C (ALT) at all times
Emergency codes: 7700 emergency, 7600 radio failure, 7500 unlawful interference, 0030 lost
Frequency Monitoring Codes show you are listening on a frequency. Reset to conspicuity afterwards
If you carry a serviceable transponder SERA requires it selected on with altitude. It can be turned off only on ATC direction, in airspace not needing carriage, or to save power
Mode S Elementary Surveillance is needed in class A or C airspace, above FL100 and in TMZs

sum.Airspace structure: Class A, CTR, CTA, TMA and airways.
sum.ATZ and aerodromes without one: 2 or 2.5 NM and 2,000 ft, plus T and U circles.
sum.MATZ: Not controlled airspace, but contact first.
sum.Requesting a transit: Request, pass message, read back and wilco.
sum.Transponder: 7000, emergency codes, FMCs and Mode S.

cards.q: ATZ radius for a runway of 1,850 m or less?
ATZ radius for a runway over 1,850 m?

cards.a: Up to 2,000 ft above the aerodrome.

cards.q: What do T and U mean on a chart circle?
cards.a: T is intensive training, U is unusual activity such as aerobatics or formation.

cards.q: Is a MATZ controlled airspace for civil aircraft?

cards.a: 5 NM radius, 3,000 ft above airfield level.

cards.q: Can you enter the ATZ within a MATZ without clearance?
Which class is a typical UK CTR?
Which class are airways and TMAs?
Where is Mode S ES required?
cards.a: Class A and C, above FL100, and TMZs.

quiz.q: The ATZ around an aerodrome with a 1,500 m runway has a radius of:
quiz.why: Runways of 1,850 m or less give a 2 NM ATZ.

o: Not controlled airspace for civilians, but contact is strongly recommended
Controlled airspace: civil aircraft need a clearance before entering
Prohibited airspace for civil aircraft while the aerodrome is open
Class A airspace, so only IFR flights may enter it with a clearance
quiz.why: Contact the unit before entering and never enter the ATZ without clearance.

quiz.q: Which class is most GA controlled airspace in the UK?
quiz.why: CTRs and CTAs are normally class D.

quiz.q: Which squawk shows a lost aircraft?
A circle with a T on the VFR chart means:
quiz.why: T denotes intensive use for training flights.

quiz.q: Mode S Elementary Surveillance is required:
o: In class A or C airspace, above FL100 and in TMZs
In class G airspace, above 3,000 ft and in ATZs
At night, above FL100 and in all controlled airspace
For IFR flights only, above FL100 and in TMZs
quiz.why: Those are the circumstances listed by the Skyway Code.
